Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Town, shops & places

exhibit verb

put on public show

also exhibited, be on show, on display, put on display, display (art), an exhibit

classical

Plin. NH 35.52: in pūblicō expōnī
Cic. Mur. 75: exposuit vāsa Samia (Lewis & Short)

expōnō, expōnere, exposuī, expositum

verb, third conjugation, transitive

to set out to be seen, to put on show

To set things out where they can be seen, in a house or in pūblicō. Its other common senses are to set forth in words, to explain, to land troops from ships, and to expose a child (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • prōpōnō, prōpōnere, prōposuī, prōpositum — to set out, to display

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.161: prōpositō argentō

    To set out in front, to display, as goods for sale (see display) or a notice in public; also to propose, to offer a prize, to set before the mind (Lewis & Short).

  • prōpalam collocāre — to put openly on show

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.161; M-O s.v. museum

    Cicero’s phrase for pictures and statues set out in a rich house; Morgan–Owens gives it for a museum’s exhibits.

  • exhibeō, exhibēre, exhibuī, exhibitum — to produce, to present; to show

    verb, second conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ov. M. 15.611 (Lewis & Short)

    Mostly to hand over or produce a person or a document (as in court), to furnish, and to keep, maintain; “show, display” is a rarer, chiefly poetic sense (Lewis & Short). Not the plain word for exhibiting art.

Examples

  • nōn explicātā veste neque prōpositō argentō neque tabulīs et signīs prōpalam conlocātīs

    with no clothes unfolded, no silver set out, no pictures and statues put openly on showCic. de Or. 1.161

  • pingī autem … mūnera atque in pūblicō expōnī coepta ā C. Terentiō Lūcānō

    the painting of [gladiatorial] shows and their exhibition in public began with Gaius Terentius LucanusPlin. NH 35.52

See also exhibition, display, museum, show, picture.

SourcesLewis & Short: expono · Lewis & Short: propono · Lewis & Short: propalam · Lewis & Short: exhibeo

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. museum.
